chapter_name: Social psychology and basic psychological treatments
chapter_title: Social psychology and basic psychological treatments

questions.question_text: Attitudes:

options.text: Are a set of beliefs which predispose an individual to particular ideas
Have affective components that are most resistant to change
Are mutually consistent and internally consistent
If situational variables are not taken into account, measured attitudes are poor predictors of behaviour

questions.explanation: The definition of attitude was given by Allport as a mental and neural state of readiness, organized through experience, exerting an influence on an individual's response to all objects and situations. Kerch and Crutchfield defined the motivational, emotional, perceptual and cognitive components. Beliefs, behaviour and affective components were identified; a change in one of these three components leads to change in the others.

questions.question_text: In measurements of attitudes:

options.text: Projective tests such as Rorschach ink blots are useful
Physiological tests such as galvanic skin response are useful
More easily administered Likert scales and visual analogue scales like semantic differential scales are useful
Thurstone scales are less sensitive than Likert scales and can have value-laden biases

questions.explanation: The Thurstone scale is dichotomous, the Likert scale is generally a five-point scale of level of agreement and the semantic differential scale is a bipolar visual analogue scale.

questions.question_text: The social effects that have an impact on measurements of behaviour are:
questions.explanation: Response set is a tendency to always agree/disagree with a set of questions. Bias to middle is avoiding extreme response. The halo effect occurs when an observer allows a preconception to influence responses. The Hawthorn effect occurs when positive social interaction between the experimenter and the subject affects response.

questions.question_text: Regarding attitudes and behaviours, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Advertising uses a central pathway requiring the consideration of new information to modify one's attitude
Advertising uses a peripheral pathway involving the presentation of cues to modify one's attitude
The characteristics of a persuasive communicator include attractive-ness and credibility
Low self-esteem and intelligence of the recipient increase the likelihood that complex communications will be persuasive
A low-anxiety recipient is more influenced by a high-fear message and vice versa

correct_answer.text: Low self-esteem and intelligence of the recipient increase the likelihood that complex communications will be persuasive

correct_answers.text: Low self-esteem and intelligence of the recipient increase the likelihood that complex communications will be persuasive

questions.explanation: Advertising uses both a and b. Other characteristics of a persuasive communicator include audience identification with the communicator, being an opinion leader, non-verbal communication, and views of reference groups. High self-esteem and intelligence of the recipient increase the likelihood that complex communications will be persuasive.

questions.question_text: Regarding persuasive influence leading to attitude change, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Message repetition can be a persuasive influence leading to attitude change
Implicit messages are more persuasive for more intelligent recipients
One-sided communications are more persuasive for those who are less intelligent
Mass media communication is more persuasive than interactive personal discussions
Social change is sometimes brought about because a few people manage to persuade the majority to change attitudes

correct_answer.text: Mass media communication is more persuasive than interactive personal discussions

correct_answers.text: Mass media communication is more persuasive than interactive personal discussions

questions.explanation: Mass media communication is less persuasive than interactive personal discussions.

questions.question_text: According to Festinger's cognitive dissonance theory, dissonance is increased by all of the following, except:

options.text: Expectation of unpleasant consequences of behaviour towards others

questions.explanation: By adding new cognitions, dissonance is decreased. Dismissing information/cognitions and changing behaviour also result in a decrease in dissonance.

questions.question_text: All of the following names are correctly paired with the appropriate concept, except:
questions.explanation: Carl Rogers was associated with the person-centred theory of personality and psychotherapy, in which the major concepts are self-actualization and self-direction. He developed client-centred therapy. Bem's self-perception theory proposes that we make judgements about ourselves using the same inferential processes and errors that we use for making judgements about others. Festinger proposed social comparison theory and Homans proposed social exchange theory.

questions.question_text: Regarding social facilitation and social inhibition, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Studies show that people performed better on the Stroop task when in the presence of others
Audience effects on performance vary depending on whether the task is very easy or difficult for the person and on how much the person feels that he /she is being evaluated
People often behave differently in a crowd than when alone, and they may experience de-individualization
Research shows that people are more likely to help a man lying on the sidewalk if many other bystanders are present
Modern warfare allows individuals to distance themselves from actual killing, giving them the feeling that they are not responsible for enemy deaths

correct_answer.text: Research shows that people are more likely to help a man lying on the sidewalk if many other bystanders are present

correct_answers.text: Research shows that people are more likely to help a man lying on the sidewalk if many other bystanders are present

questions.explanation: Research shows that people are more likely to help a man lying on the sidewalk if no other bystanders are present.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about factors relating to interpersonal attraction are true, except:

options.text: Neighbours are likely to form a friendship simply because of proximity
People prefer relationships that appear to have an optimum cost:benefit ratio
Complimentarity is more important than similarity, although the latter increases in importance with time
Partners in successful long-term relationships tend to be similar to each other in characteristics such as age, race, education and physical attractiveness
In later life, the passionate component of romantic love tends to become less important than the companionate component

correct_answer.text: Complimentarity is more important than similarity, although the latter increases in importance with time

correct_answers.text: Complimentarity is more important than similarity, although the latter increases in importance with time

questions.explanation: Similarity is more important than complimentarity, although the latter increases in importance with time.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about theories relating to interpersonal issues and intergroup behaviour, except:

options.text: According to Heider's attribution theory, internal (dispositional) attribution is the inference that the person is primarily responsible for the action
Primary attribution error is a bias towards situational rather than dispositional attribution when inferring the cause of other people's behaviour
Stereotypes persist even if data do not confirm them
Stereotypes can become self-perpetuating and self-fulfilling
Prejudiced individuals may behave in ways that create stereotyped behaviour, which sustain their prejudice

correct_answer.text: Primary attribution error is a bias towards situational rather than dispositional attribution when inferring the cause of other people's behaviour

correct_answers.text: Primary attribution error is a bias towards situational rather than dispositional attribution when inferring the cause of other people's behaviour

questions.explanation: Primary attribution error is a bias towards dispositional rather than situational attribution when inferring the cause of other people's behaviour.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about observations related to social influence, except:

options.text: Autocratic leadership is useful in urgent situations
Laissez-faire is appropriate for creative and person-oriented tasks
Audience effect is the social facilitation occurring when others simply observe
Intelligent, expressive and socially effective individuals are most vulnerable to group pressure

correct_answer.text: Intelligent, expressive and socially effective individuals are most vulnerable to group pressure

correct_answers.text: Intelligent, expressive and socially effective individuals are most vulnerable to group pressure

questions.explanation: Intelligent, expressive and socially effective individuals are least vulnerable to group pressure.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about theories of social influence, except:

options.text: French and Raven observed that social power could be derived from skill, knowledge, experience and power to punish
Normative social influence can lead to an individual's agreeing with a group even if the individual holds a different personal view
Conformity pressures increase with group size up to a maximum of three
Informational social influence is more evident with ambiguous stimuli
Milgram demonstrated that obedience is affected by proximity to the victim, with decreased obedience with distance

correct_answer.text: Informational social influence is more evident with ambiguous stimuli

correct_answers.text: Informational social influence is more evident with ambiguous stimuli

questions.explanation: Milgram demonstrated that obedience is affected by proximity to the victim, with increased obedience with distance. French and Raven described five types of social power: authority, reward, coercive, referent and expert. Deutsch and Gerard described two types of conformity: informational and normative.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about groupthink, except:

options.text: It may include collective rationalization and 'mindguards'
It may lead to decisions that are based on incomplete information
It is helpful in preventing decisions that have failed to fully examine all the risks and consider alternative plans
It can be guarded against by having open debates
It can be guarded against by appointing a 'devil's advocate' or using external experts

correct_answer.text: It is helpful in preventing decisions that have failed to fully examine all the risks and consider alternative plans

correct_answers.text: It is helpful in preventing decisions that have failed to fully examine all the risks and consider alternative plans

questions.explanation: Groupthink is the desire to achieve consensus and avoid dissent in group decisions. Mindguards are individuals who are self-appointed to prevent the group from considering information that would challenge the effectiveness of the group. Groupthink leads to decisions that have failed to examine fully all the risks and to consider alternative plans.

questions.question_text: All of the following disorders are more likely to be diagnosed in lower social classes, except:
questions.explanation: Depression in women and deliberate self-harm are also more likely to be diagnosed in lower social classes, whereas anorexia and bulimia in females are more likely to be diagnosed in upper classes.

questions.question_text: Regarding social, family factors in relation to illnesses, all of the following names are correctly paired with their related concept, except:

options.text: Vaughn and Leff–Marital skew and marital schism

correct_answer.text: Vaughn and Leff–Marital skew and marital schism

correct_answers.text: Vaughn and Leff–Marital skew and marital schism

questions.explanation: The concept of marital skew and marital schism was proposed by Lidz. Vaughn and Leff, and Brown are associated with expressed emotion and Wynne is associated with abnormal family communication.

questions.question_text: Regarding effects of expressed emotion, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Comments expressing unambiguous dislike or disapproval are associated with high expressed emotion and predict relapse of schizophrenia
Emotional over-involvement is associated with high expressed emotion and predict relapse of schizophrenia
Positive remarks expressing praise or approval of the patient are not associated with high expressed emotion
Follow-up studies have confirmed that, in the presence of high expressed emotion in the family, the relapse rates of treated and untreated patients with schizophrenia are almost the same
High expressed emotion at home is associated with an increased risk of relapse of depression

correct_answer.text: Follow-up studies have confirmed that, in the presence of high expressed emotion in the family, the relapse rates of treated and untreated patients with schizophrenia are almost the same

correct_answers.text: Follow-up studies have confirmed that, in the presence of high expressed emotion in the family, the relapse rates of treated and untreated patients with schizophrenia are almost the same

questions.explanation: Vaughn and Leff observed that, in the presence of high expressed emotion, the relapse rate was higher in untreated patients than that in treated patients.

questions.question_text: The four vulnerability factors identified by Brown and Harris that make women more susceptible to depression following life events do not include:

options.text: The loss of their mother before the age of 11 years
The lack of a confiding relationship
Having three or more children under the age of 15 years at home

questions.explanation: High expressed emotion can be associated with relapse of depression.

questions.question_text: On the Holmes and Rahe social readjustment scale, which of the following life events was given the highest life change value?

options.text: Death of a close family member

questions.explanation: The highest life change value is for death of spouse, the values going from a to e in decreasing order.

questions.question_text: Studies observed a clear relationship between life events and all of the following conditions, except:

options.text: Functional disorders presenting physically without an organic cause

questions.explanation: Brown, Birley and T ennant observed that independent life events are more likely to occur before relapse rather than before first onset of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following names is associated with studies related to the concept of institutionalization?
questions.explanation: A total institution is an organization in which a large number of like-situated individuals, cut off from the wider social world for an appreciable time together, lead an enclosed, formally administered way of life.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man was clearly told about the bad prognosis of his wife's cancer in the previous outpatient appointment a month ago, but he tells you that he does not have any memory of that conversation. The possible defence mechanism involved is:
questions.explanation: Denial is the refusal to recognize external reality, and repression is the process by which thoughts that the conscious mind finds unacceptable are repressed from consciousness.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old man who had strong sexual fantasies towards another woman attributed his impulses and desires to his wife and became extremely jealous and possessive of her. The possible defence mechanism involved is:
questions.explanation: Projection means that unacceptable qualities, feelings, thoughts or wishes are projected on to another person or thing.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old woman diagnosed with personality disorder walked out of the ward round room after becoming argumentative, and on her way out she kicked a chair in the corridor. The possible defence mechanism involved is:
questions.explanation: Displacement means that emotions, ideas or wishes are transferred from their original object to a more acceptable substitute.

questions.question_text: On an assessment for psychotherapy it was formulated that a 24-year-old woman with obsessive compulsive disorder was secretly fascinated with urine; she started rejecting and denying all interest in urine and developed an obsessive need for cleaning her hands. The possible defence mechanism involved is:
questions.explanation: Magical undoing and isolation are other defence mechanisms associated with obsessive compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man with obsessive compulsive disorder tells you that by touching lamp posts in a specific order he attempts to recreate the past so that he can avoid some horrible things he is worried about. If the particular order is missed he needs to start again from the beginning. The possible defence mechanism is:
questions.explanation: The attempt to undo has a magical quality and aims to reverse the reality of the original hostile thought or wish and recreate the past as if such intentions never existed.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about psychoanalysis, except:

options.text: The primary focus is on analyst and intrasession events
Symptom relief is an indirect result

questions.explanation: Regression is encouraged. The basic goals are structural reorganization of personality, resolution of unconscious conflicts, and insight into intrapsychic events. Symptom relief is an indirect result.

questions.question_text: In an expressive form of psychotherapy, the therapist said to the patient, who was late, 'Perhaps the reason you are late is that you were afraid I would react the way your father reacted to the success you are now having.' The psychotherapeutic intervention used here is:
questions.explanation: Interpretation involves making something conscious that was previously unconscious.

questions.question_text: In Freud's interpretation of dreams, which of the following mechanisms was considered as facilitating the discharge of latent impulses?
questions.explanation: Condensation means that several unconscious impulses, wishes or feelings can be combined and attached to one manifest dream image; displacement means that energy associated with one object is diverted to a substitute object (projection was described as a special type of displacement); symbolic representation means that highly charged ideas will be represented by innocent images. Through secondary revision, primitive aspects of the dreams are organized to a more clear form.

questions.question_text: All the following names are correctly paired with the form of brief psychotherapy associated with their work, except:
questions.explanation: Dialectical therapy was developed by Linehan. Anthony Ryle developed cognitive analytic therapy.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are correct regarding cognitive analytic therapy, except:

options.text: It involves reformulation, the patient being helped to recognize the recurrences of unrevised patterns, and is open to revision
It describes traps as negative assumptions that generate acts that produce consequences and reinforce assumptions
It describes dilemmas as a person acting on false dichotomies, usually unaware that this is the case
It describes snags as the abandonment of appropriate roles because of the assumption that others will oppose them
It requires very well structured sessions with diagrams and homework until the end of the therapy

correct_answer.text: It requires very well structured sessions with diagrams and homework until the end of the therapy

correct_answers.text: It requires very well structured sessions with diagrams and homework until the end of the therapy

questions.explanation: At the fourth session the therapist provides a summary of his /her understanding of the history and its meaning, and describes the maladaptive strategies (a diagram may be used). The patient feels understood and held and becomes less defensive. Sessions thereafter are usually unstructured, although homework is given.

questions.question_text: Transference:

options.text: May help patients to learn more about themselves

questions.explanation: Transference is the displacement of attitudes and feelings originally experienced in relationships with people from the past onto the analyst.

questions.question_text: Regarding small-group therapy, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It can be used to modify personality problems
It has specific goals, i.e. high leader activity includes cognitive behavioural therapy carried out in a group setting
Yalom's curative factors in a group treatment include selective abstraction
Results are generally thought to be better with patients who are young, well motivated and free from personality disorder
Severe social anxiety is a contraindication

correct_answer.text: Yalom's curative factors in a group treatment include selective abstraction

correct_answers.text: Yalom's curative factors in a group treatment include selective abstraction

questions.explanation: Yalom's curative factors include interpersonal learning, catharsis, group cohesiveness, insight, development of socializing techniques, existential awareness, universality, instillation of hope, altruism, corrective recapitulation of family group, guidance, and imitative behaviour.

questions.question_text: All of the following are contraindications to the therapeutic community method of treatment, except:
questions.explanation: In a therapeutic community there are usually 20–30 members, who usually stay for 9–18 months. Main indications for therapeutic community are dissocial personality disorder and unstable personality disorder.

questions.question_text: The principal features of a therapeutic community include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Members learn about themselves through the reactions of other members, mutual help, directness and honesty. Group meetings are another principal feature.

questions.question_text: In cognitive psychotherapy, disattribution technique is most useful as an intervention to identify and correct the following cognitive error:
questions.explanation: Excessive responsibility is associated with assumption of personal causality, e.g. 'I am responsible for all bad things'.

questions.question_text: The key element of supportive therapy is:
questions.explanation: The therapeutic relationship, listening, emotional release, information and advice, encouraging hope and persuasion are all important elements of supportive psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about functional analysis are true, except:

options.text: Problem clarification is an important component of functional analysis
Motivational analysis is an important component of functional analysis
Developmental analysis is an important component of functional analysis
Transactional analysis is an important component of functional analysis
Exploration of social relationships is an important component of functional analysis

correct_answer.text: Transactional analysis is an important component of functional analysis

correct_answers.text: Transactional analysis is an important component of functional analysis

questions.explanation: The frequency and intensity of the problem situation, the patient's self-control, and the patient's environment are also assessed.

questions.question_text: The cognitive distortions in depression identified by Beck include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Cognitive therapy for depression was developed by AT Beck.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old woman with anxiety was given a prompt card by her therapist. On the card a reassuring thought was written: 'My heart is beating fast because I feel anxious, not because I have heart disease'. This is an example of which cognitive technique?
questions.explanation: Neutralizing involves rehearsing a reassuring response to reduce anxiety.

questions.question_text: Social skills training was found to be helpful in:
questions.explanation: Social skills training is useful when skills may have been lost, possibly through disuse, in patients with chronic mental illness.

questions.question_text: The following names are correctly paired with the form of therapy they have developed, except:
questions.explanation: Berne is associated with transactional analysis and Moreno with psychodrama.

questions.question_text: Couple therapy is not recommended in all the following scenarios, except:

options.text: When there is conflict about one of the partner's sexual life
When one of the partners suffers from a severe form of psychosis
When one or both partners want to divorce
When one spouse refuses to participate because of anxiety
When one spouse refuses to participate because of fear

correct_answer.text: When there is conflict about one of the partner's sexual life

correct_answers.text: When there is conflict about one of the partner's sexual life

questions.explanation: When marital problems result from conflict arising from a partner's sexual life, couple therapy is indicated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a mature defence mechanism?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is changing a socially objectionable aim to a socially acceptable one.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about transference, except:

options.text: It refers to the therapist's attitude towards the patient
It is a repetition of reactions originating in regard to significant persons in early childhood
It could be an agent for therapeutic change

correct_answer.text: It refers to the therapist's attitude towards the patient

correct_answers.text: It refers to the therapist's attitude towards the patient

questions.explanation: Transference is shifting an emotional attitude from a past object or person to the therapist.

questions.question_text: The characteristic regime in a therapeutic community as described by Rapoport includes:
questions.explanation: The role of staff is to ensure a basic structure within which members of the community can interact.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true statements about psychoanalytic theory that explains obsessive symptoms, except:

options.text: Obsessional symptoms result from unconscious impulses of an aggressive nature
Obsessional symptoms result from unconscious impulses of a sexual nature
Anxiety is reduced by the action of defence mechanism of repression
Anxiety is reduced by the action of defence mechanism of reaction formation
Obsessional symptoms occur when there is a regression to the oral stage of development

correct_answer.text: Obsessional symptoms occur when there is a regression to the oral stage of development

correct_answers.text: Obsessional symptoms occur when there is a regression to the oral stage of development

questions.explanation: Obsessional symptoms occur when there is a regression to the anal stage of development.

questions.question_text: All of the following defence mechanisms are paired with the condition associated with them, except:
questions.explanation: Magical undoing is associated with obsessive compulsive disorder, and depression with turning against oneself and regression to the oral stage.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of acute conversion disorder, it is recommended that:

options.text: Confrontation is almost always necessary to avoid reinforcement of disability and symptoms
A complete physical examination and investigation should not be attempted as it may reinforce the symptoms
Positive reassurance and praising healthy behaviour help to avoid reinforcement of disability and symptoms
The patient should not be provided with a face-saving opportunity as it may lead to reinforcement of disability and symptoms

correct_answer.text: Positive reassurance and praising healthy behaviour help to avoid reinforcement of disability and symptoms

correct_answers.text: Positive reassurance and praising healthy behaviour help to avoid reinforcement of disability and symptoms

questions.explanation: Confrontation is not recommended; full physical examinations and investigations are necessary to rule out organic causes as well as to exclude serious medical problems. Positive reassurance and praising healthy behaviour offer the patient a face-saving opportunity for rapid return to normal physical functioning.

questions.question_text: Regarding cognitive behaviour therapy, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It is designed to change cognitions and behaviour directly
It is concerned with the way the disorder has developed
It focuses on the factors that are maintaining the disorder at the time of treatment
The patient is an active partner
Therapeutic procedures are usually presented as experiments

correct_answer.text: It is concerned with the way the disorder has developed

correct_answers.text: It is concerned with the way the disorder has developed

questions.explanation: Cognitive behaviour therapy differs from dynamic psychotherapy in that it is not concerned with the way the disorder is developed.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman who believes that she will faint during a panic attack tells you that she tenses her muscles every time she feels anxious, because she is convinced that she would have fainted had she not done this on every occasion. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: People develop safety behaviour as a way of reducing their immediate concerns but the long-term effect is to perpetuate the concerns.
